title: Moovalur Ramamirtham: ₹1,000/Month for TN Girls
meta_description: Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar scheme gives ₹1,000/month to TN girls who studied in govt schools. No income limit. Apply online at penkalvi.tn.gov.in.

hero.one_liner: Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar scheme (Pudhumai Penn) pays Rs 1,000 a month to TN girls who studied in government schools, with no income limit. Apply online.

what_is_it: The Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme is a Tamil Nadu government programme that pays ₹1,000 every month to girl students who studied in government schools and are now pursuing higher education. It is administered by the Department of Social Welfare and Women Empowerment, Government of Tamil Nadu, and is also widely known as the Pudhumai Penn Scheme or the Pen Kalvi Scheme.
Unlike most scholarship schemes in India, this scheme has no income ceiling at all. A girl's family does not need to fall below a poverty line or provide a family income certificate to qualify.

eligibility.label: School history
eligibility.value: Studied Class 6 to 12 in a Tamil Nadu government or government-aided school.

eligibility.label: Income limit
eligibility.value: None. There is no family income ceiling.

eligibility.label: Current study
eligibility.value: Enrolled in a recognised first higher education course (UG, diploma, ITI).

eligibility.label: Bank
eligibility.value: Active account at Indian Bank, Canara Bank, Indian Overseas Bank, or SBI.

eligibility_filters.notes: Girls who studied Class 6-12 in TN government or government-aided schools, now in a recognised first higher education course. No income limit. RTE Class 6-8 private plus 9-12 government also eligible.

how_to_apply.title: Confirm Your Eligibility
how_to_apply.description: Verify that you studied from 6th standard to 12th standard in a Tamil Nadu government school, meaning a government, corporation, municipal, panchayat union, adi dravidar and tribal welfare, Kallar Reclamation, forest department, social welfare department, or RTE-admission school. Also confirm that you are now enrolled in a recognised first higher education course at an institution in Tamil Nadu. There is no income ceiling, and students who already receive other scholarships are still eligible. Distance education and courses outside Tamil Nadu are not covered.

how_to_apply.title: Open an Account at One of the Four Designated Banks
how_to_apply.description: You must have an active bank account at Indian Bank, Canara Bank, Indian Overseas Bank, or State Bank of India for the monthly DBT payment to work. If you do not already have an account at one of these four banks, ask your college help desk to assist you in opening a zero-balance account before you begin registration. The bank will provide a debit card so you can withdraw the ₹1,000 monthly amount from any ATM once payments start.

how_to_apply.title: Link Aadhaar to Your Bank Account
how_to_apply.description: Before registering on the portal, ensure your Aadhaar number is seeded to your bank account and that the name on Aadhaar matches the name on your bank account exactly. Tamil names often have multiple English transliterations, and even a one-letter discrepancy will block the DBT transfer after approval. Visit your bank branch to update the account name or Aadhaar seeding if needed before proceeding. Aadhaar linking is mandatory for the scheme to work.

how_to_apply.title: Register at penkalvi.tn.gov.in
how_to_apply.description: Open penkalvi.tn.gov.in on your phone or computer. The portal is available in Tamil and English. Click Student Registration and enter your mobile number. Verify it with the OTP. Fill in your personal details, your EMIS number from school (the portal auto-fetches your school history using this), your current college name and course, and your bank account number with IFSC code. Preview the details before submission and correct any errors. The portal confirms your registration by SMS with a unique application ID after successful submission.

how_to_apply.title: College Verification and Sanction
how_to_apply.description: After you submit, your college nodal officer logs into the portal on the institution side and verifies your enrollment. The verified application is forwarded to the Directorate of Social Welfare, which sanctions the incentive amount. You receive an SMS when the sanction is confirmed. The first ₹1,000 reaches your bank account within a few weeks of sanction. If your college is not yet registered on penkalvi.tn.gov.in, ask your college administration to register as an institution before you try to submit your application.

how_to_apply.title: Keep Your Bonafide Certification Up to Date
how_to_apply.description: Once payments start, ₹1,000 arrives automatically on the 7th of every month. To keep receiving it, your college must certify your bonafide student status twice a year: before June 30 and before December 31. If your college misses a certification window, payments are paused until the next cycle. Remind your college nodal officer well before each deadline. If you change colleges, update your details on the portal immediately so your new institution can certify you from their side.

ministry: Social Welfare and Women Empowerment Department, Government of Tamil Nadu

extra_sections.heading: What Is the Moovalur Ramamirtham Scheme
content: The scheme is named after Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar, a Tamil social reformer and independence activist who fought against child marriage and for women's education in early twentieth-century Tamil Nadu. Naming the scheme after her signals its purpose: every girl who reaches higher education should have the financial means to stay there and complete her degree.

Payments are made through Direct Benefit Transfer via the IFHRMS system, and the money reaches your Aadhaar-linked bank account on the 7th of each month. Once registered and verified, the transfer happens automatically every month without any re-application or monthly form submission.
The only requirements are that she studied in a government school from the 6th standard onward and is now enrolled in a recognised course at a Tamil Nadu institution.

extra_sections.title: The Marriage Scheme Became an Education Scheme
extra_sections.content:
The old Moovalur Ramamirtham marriage assistance scheme no longer exists. In the 2022-23 budget it was transformed into this higher education assurance scheme.

The state decided a monthly stipend during college does more to delay early marriage than a one-time grant at the wedding. If you are searching for the marriage grant, this education scheme is what replaced it.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible
content: The scheme covers a wide range of higher education options: three-year, four-year, and five-year undergraduate degree programmes in arts, science, engineering, agriculture, medicine, and law; polytechnic diploma programmes of one to three years; ITI certificate courses of at least one year; paramedical courses; and combined post-graduation programmes for the first three years. Any first higher education course at a recognised institution in Tamil Nadu qualifies.

There is no limit on how many girls from a single family can benefit simultaneously. If four sisters all studied in government schools and all enrol in college, all four can receive the monthly ₹1,000 at the same time.
The government deliberately removed any per-family cap to avoid penalising households where multiple daughters are pursuing education at once.

extra_sections.heading: Courses and the First-Course Rule
content: Correspondence courses, distance education programmes, and courses at unrecognised institutions are explicitly excluded. Cross-border students who completed schooling in other states and came to Tamil Nadu for college are also not eligible.
The scheme is designed specifically for girls whose entire school journey was within Tamil Nadu's government school system.

Each girl is eligible only for her first course of higher education. If you completed your UG degree and received incentive payments throughout, you cannot apply again for a second degree, a second diploma, or a PG programme.
The incentive supports entry into higher education, not indefinite continuation across multiple qualifications.

extra_sections.title: One of the Few Schemes With No Ceiling
extra_sections.desc:
Unlike most scholarships, this scheme has no family income limit at all.

Any girl who studied in a Tamil Nadu government school and is now in her first higher education course qualifies, and she can receive it on top of other scholarships.

extra_sections.heading: Government and Aided Schools Both Count
content: The scheme was launched during the 2022-23 Tamil Nadu budget announcement, when the Finance Minister noted that girls from government schools had a significantly lower enrollment ratio in higher education compared to girls from private schools. The scheme directly addresses this gap by removing the cost barrier that stops girls from joining college after Class 12.

Nearly six lakh girl students can potentially benefit each year according to government projections when the scheme was announced, and ₹698 crore was allocated in the initial budget. The scale reflects how many government school graduates in Tamil Nadu are now at the threshold of higher education.

extra_sections.heading: Applying on the Pudhumai Penn Portal
content: The official portal for this scheme is penkalvi.tn.gov.in. It is available in both Tamil and English and works on mobile as well as desktop.
You can register directly as a student using your mobile number and OTP, or your college may register you as part of a bulk enrollment for all eligible students in the institution.

Your EMIS (Educational Management Information System) number from your school connects your portal registration to your government school history automatically. The portal fetches your school records from the EMIS database to confirm that you attended a Tamil Nadu government school from 6th standard onward.
This is how the system verifies school eligibility without requiring a separate school certificate in most cases.

steps.title: Confirm eligibility
steps.desc: You must have studied Class 6 to 12 in a TN government or government-aided school and now be in a recognised first higher education course.

steps.title: Register on the portal
steps.desc: Go to pudhumaipenn.tn.gov.in, register with your mobile and OTP, then enter your EMIS number, Aadhaar, and college details.

steps.title: Add bank and school history
steps.desc: Enter your account at one of the four core banks and fill your school details from Class 6 to 12, then submit.

steps.title: College verifies twice a year
steps.desc: Your college certifies your bonafide status on 30 June and 31 December. The first payment can take three to four weeks after verification.

extra_sections.title: Two Portals: Which One to Use
extra_sections.content:
New applications now go through pudhumaipenn.tn.gov.in, usually via your college. The older penkalvi.tn.gov.in is used only to track old applications.

If your college guides you to register, follow their portal link. Contact your college principal if you are unsure which applies to you.

extra_sections.heading: The EMIS Number and Bank Account
content: If you do not have an EMIS number, which can happen if you attended multiple schools with incomplete record updates or were admitted under RTE without full data entry, the portal has a pathway for manual verification. You submit your complete school details and supporting documents, and the Commissioner of School Education verifies them.
This takes up to fifteen working days.
Aadhaar is mandatory. Your Aadhaar number must be entered during registration and your bank account must be seeded with the same Aadhaar number for DBT to work.
A mismatch between your Aadhaar name and your bank account name, even a single letter difference in the transliteration of a Tamil name, will block the transfer after approval.

items.title: UG degrees
items.sub: Three, four, and five-year undergraduate degree programmes at recognised colleges and universities are covered.

items.title: Diploma and ITI
items.sub: Polytechnic diplomas and ITI courses qualify, paid till the course is completed without interruption.

items.title: Excluded courses
items.sub: Correspondence, distance education, open university, and unrecognised institutions are explicitly excluded.

items.title: First course only
items.sub: Only your first higher education course counts. A second degree after receiving the incentive does not qualify.

extra_sections.heading: Documents and First Payment
content: Documents required for registration include your Aadhaar card, your college admission letter or bonafide certificate confirming your current course, and your bank account details showing the account number and IFSC code. If your EMIS verification is manual, you will also need school records such as a transfer certificate or mark sheets showing government school attendance from 6th standard.

The first payment after initial approval may take three to four weeks from the date your college submits enrollment verification. Once active, ₹1,000 arrives in your account on the 7th of every subsequent month without any further action from you.

items.title: EMIS number
items.sub: Your school EMIS number links your registration to your school records. Without it, registration takes longer but you are not disqualified.

items.title: Aadhaar mandatory
items.sub: Your Aadhaar must be entered and seeded to your bank account, or the DBT payment will fail.

items.title: Designated bank account
items.sub: Use an account at Indian Bank, Canara Bank, Indian Overseas Bank, or SBI. Private or cooperative bank accounts do not work.

items.title: Admission proof
items.sub: Your college admission letter or bonafide certificate confirming your current course and year.

extra_sections.heading: How the Payment Cycle Works
content: The college or institution you attend plays a continuing role throughout the scheme. It certifies twice a year, on June 30 and December 31, that you are still enrolled and actively continuing your education.
Payments for students who cannot be certified are paused until the next certification window, making timely college cooperation essential.
Your college is also your first point of contact for grievances. If a payment is late or missing, or if there is a data mismatch, report it to your college nodal officer first.
For issues the college cannot resolve, you can file an online grievance directly through the grievance section on penkalvi.tn.gov.in.

extra_sections.title: Why Payments Stop and How to Fix It
extra_sections.content:
The most common reason payments stop is a missed bonafide certification by your college. The college must certify your status twice a year.

An Aadhaar name mismatch with your bank account is the other frequent cause. Match the names exactly and confirm your college has certified you for the term.

extra_sections.heading: If a Payment Is Missing
content: The most common reason payments stop after running for several months is a missed bonafide certification. Your college must certify your continued enrollment before June 30 and before December 31 every year.

If the nodal officer misses the deadline or submits late, payments pause until the next cycle. Track your certification status on the portal and remind your college nodal officer at least two weeks before each deadline, not on the day of the deadline.

An Aadhaar name mismatch with the bank account is the single most common cause of payment failure after approval. Tamil names transliterate differently across documents and even a single letter difference blocks the DBT transfer.

Visit your bank branch before registering on the portal and verify that the account name matches your Aadhaar name exactly. If not, update the bank account name rather than the Aadhaar name, since Aadhaar corrections take longer.

items.title: Wrong bank
items.sub: DBT routes only through the four core banks. Private or cooperative bank accounts block the payment.

items.title: No EMIS number
items.sub: Students without an EMIS number can still apply, but the school history must be verified manually, which takes longer.

items.title: Private college confusion
items.sub: Private college students are eligible if they studied Class 6-12 in a government school. The college type now does not matter.

items.title: Gap year
items.sub: Girls who did not join college immediately after Class 12 can still apply once they enrol. There is no time-gap bar.

extra_sections.heading: Transfers, Gap Years and Second Degrees
content: Gap year students who did not immediately join college after Class 12 can still apply once they enrol. There is no time limit from Class 12 completion to applying.
A year or two between school and college does not disqualify you, as long as your government school history remains intact and you are now enrolled in a first recognised course.

If you transfer from one college to another during your course, update your college details on the portal immediately. The old institution will mark you inactive in its next certification cycle if you are no longer on their rolls.
When that happens, payments stop. The new institution must be registered on penkalvi.tn.gov.in for its certification to count, so confirm this with your new college before or right after joining.

extra_sections.text: The Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar scheme is one of the few in India with no income ceiling. Any girl who went to a Tamil Nadu government school and is now in college qualifies. Every ₹1,000 arrives on the 7th of the month, directly in her bank account, without any re-application or monthly renewal.

extra_sections.heading: Grievances and College Support
content: Unresolved grievances can be escalated through the online grievance mechanism on penkalvi.tn.gov.in. After logging in, navigate to the grievance section, describe your issue clearly with your application ID, and submit.

The State Programme Management Unit under the Social Welfare department monitors all open grievances and is required to escalate to the relevant district social welfare officer if the issue is not resolved at the college level.

If you transfer from one registered institution to another during your course, update your college details on the portal immediately after the transfer is confirmed. The old institution will certify you as inactive in the next cycle if you are no longer on their rolls, which pauses payments.
The new institution must also be registered on the portal for their certification to count.

faqs.question: What is the Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme?
faqs.answer:
It is a Tamil Nadu government scheme run by the Department of Social Welfare and Women Empowerment that pays ₹1,000 per month to girl students who studied from 6th to 12th standard in Tamil Nadu government schools and are now enrolled in a recognised first higher education course at an institution in Tamil Nadu. Also called the Pudhumai Penn Scheme or Pen Kalvi Scheme, the money goes to the student's bank account on the 7th of each month via DBT.

There is no income limit, and receiving other scholarships does not disqualify you.

faqs.question: How do I apply for the Moovalur Ramamirtham higher education scheme online?
faqs.answer:
Go to penkalvi.tn.gov.in on your phone or computer and click Student Registration. Enter your mobile number and verify with OTP.

Fill in your EMIS number, current college and course details, and bank account details (Indian Bank, Canara Bank, Indian Overseas Bank, or SBI only). After submission, your college verifies your enrollment and forwards the application to the Directorate of Social Welfare.

Once sanctioned, ₹1,000 arrives in your bank account on the 7th of each month automatically. You can also register through your college if they do bulk enrollments.

faqs.question: Is there an income limit for the Moovalur Ramamirtham scholarship?
faqs.answer:
No. There is no family income ceiling for this scheme. This makes it unusual among government scholarship programmes in India.

Any girl who studied in a Tamil Nadu government school from 6th standard and is now enrolled in a recognised higher education course qualifies, regardless of what her family earns. She does not need to submit a family income certificate.

She can also receive this ₹1,000 per month simultaneously with any other scholarship she already holds.

faqs.question: What happened to the Moovalur Ramamirtham marriage scheme?
faqs.answer:
The Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Ninaivu Marriage Assistance Scheme was discontinued in 2022-23. The Tamil Nadu government replaced it with the Higher Education Assurance Scheme, reasoning that a monthly stipend during college does more to prevent early marriage than a one-time grant at the wedding.

The budget previously allocated to marriage assistance was redirected to the monthly incentive for girl students. There is no separate marriage assistance scheme under this name any longer.

faqs.question: Which courses are eligible and which are excluded under this scheme?
faqs.answer:
Eligible courses include all undergraduate degrees (arts, science, engineering, medicine, agriculture, law), polytechnic diploma programmes of one to three years, ITI certificate courses of at least one year, and paramedical courses at recognised institutions in Tamil Nadu. For combined post-graduation programmes, only the first three years qualify.

Not eligible: distance education, correspondence courses, courses at unrecognised institutions, courses outside Tamil Nadu, and any second degree or second diploma (only the first higher education course counts).

faqs.question: Can I apply if I am at a private college?
faqs.answer:
Yes. The eligibility condition is based on your school history, not the type of college you now attend.

If you studied in a Tamil Nadu government school from 6th to 12th standard, you can apply even if you are currently at a private aided or self-financing college. The college must be a recognised institution in Tamil Nadu and must be registered on penkalvi.tn.gov.in.

Most recognised colleges in Tamil Nadu are already registered. Ask your college nodal officer if you are unsure whether your institution is listed.

faqs.question: How do I check my Moovalur Ramamirtham application status?
faqs.answer:
Log in to penkalvi.tn.gov.in with your registered mobile number. The portal shows your application status at each stage from submission to sanction.

You also receive SMS alerts when the application moves forward. If the portal shows pending for more than four weeks after submission, check with your college nodal officer to confirm they have completed the enrollment verification step on the college portal.

The nodal officer can see the application's current stage from the institution's side and identify any hold.

faqs.question: What do I do if my monthly payment has not arrived on the 7th?
faqs.answer:
Check three things first: that your bank account is active (not dormant), that your Aadhaar is correctly seeded to your account, and that your college has submitted the bonafide certification for the current half-year. A dormant account, a broken Aadhaar seeding link, or a missed college certification are the three most common causes of stopped payments.

Log in to penkalvi.tn.gov.in to check your status, and contact your college nodal officer to verify the certification. For issues that remain unresolved, use the online grievance mechanism on the portal.
